item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
725
ABPZ20 KNHC 212319
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 PM PDT Wed Oct 21 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on recently
upgraded Tropical Storm Vance, located several hundred miles
south of Acapulco, Mexico.

Western Central Pacific:
An area of low pressure is forecast to form near the International
Date Line, a few hundred miles west-southwest of Johnston Atoll
late this weekend or early next week. Environmental conditions
appear conducive for some gradual development thereafter while the
system moves generally eastward to east-northeastward.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...30 percent.

&&
Public advisories on Tropical Storm Vance are issued under WMO
header WTPZ32 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCPEP2.
Forecast/advisories on Tropical Storm Vance are issued under WMO
header WTPZ22 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCMEP2.

$$
Forecaster Pasch

item.title: Summary for Tropical Storm Vance (EP2/EP222026)
item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)
item.description: ...VANCE STRENGTHENS SLIGHTLY... ...FORECAST TO RAPIDLY INTENSIFY... As of 9:00 PM CST Wed Oct 21 the center of Vance was located near 9.6, -100.7 with movement WNW at 5 mph. The minimum central pressure was 1000 mb with maximum sustained winds of about 45 mph.

item.title: Tropical Storm Vance Public Advisory Number 3
item.description:
Issued at 900 PM CST Wed Oct 21 2026 
000
WTPZ32 KNHC 220257
TCPEP2
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Vance Advisory Number   3
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP222026
900 PM CST Wed Oct 21 2026
 
...VANCE STRENGTHENS SLIGHTLY...
...FORECAST TO RAPIDLY INTENSIFY...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 900 PM CST...0300 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...9.6N 100.7W
ABOUT 505 MI...815 KM S OF ACAPULCO MEXICO
ABOUT 690 MI...1115 KM SSE OF MANZANILLO MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...45 MPH...75 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WNW OR 290 DEGREES AT 5 MPH...7 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1000 MB...29.53 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 900 PM CST (0300 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Vance was
located near latitude 9.6 North, longitude 100.7 West. Vance is
moving toward the west-northwest near 5 mph (7 km/h) and is expected
to turn northwestward, then north-northwestward over the next few
days, with a slight decrease in forward speed.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 45 mph (75 km/h) with higher gusts.
Rapid intensification is expected, and the system is forecast to 
become a hurricane on Thursday.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 70 miles (110 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1000 mb (29.53 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF: Swells generated by Vance are expected to begin affecting
portions of the coast of southern and southwestern Mexico this
weekend and continue into next week. These swells are likely to
cause life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Please
consult products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 300 AM CST.
 
$$
Forecaster Pierce/Gibbs
item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)

item.title: Tropical Storm Vance Forecast Discussion Number 2
item.description:
Issued at 300 PM CST Wed Oct 21 2026 
000
WTPZ42 KNHC 212033
TCDEP2
 
Tropical Storm Vance Discussion Number   2
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP222026
300 PM CST Wed Oct 21 2026
 
Satellite imagery shows that the system continues to produce deep
convection in improved banding features, as depicted in recent
microwave images. An earlier scatterometer pass shortly after the
previous advisory showed that the low-level center was slightly
farther south and had a peak wind of 27 kt. The latest satellite
intensity estimates from UW-CIMSS and TAFB are 32-35 kt, and using
these estimates, the initial intensity is raised to 35 kt for this
advisory, making the system Tropical Storm Vance.
 
The initial motion is estimated at 265/6 kt. A generally slow 
forward motion is expected with a turn toward the northwest and then 
north-northwest as the cyclone is steered along the southern and 
western periphery of a mid-level ridge located over Mexico. There 
continues to be some disagreement in the short term over when the 
turn toward the northwest will occur The GFS and hurricane regional 
models continue to show a southwest motion, while the HCCA and GDMI 
show the system slowing and turning sooner. The latest NHC track 
forecast is closest to the HCCA and GDMI, the best-performing models 
this season, and was shifted slightly to the right compared to the 
previous one.
 
Vance is within a conducive environment for steady to rapid 
intensification (RI), with warm sea surface temperatures near 
29-30C, low wind shear, and favorable upper-level divergence. RI 
SHIPS and DTOPS guidance remains very bullish, showing RI over the 
next 12-60 hours. The NHC intensity forecast follows suit and the 
peak intensity was increased slightly from the previous one, 
although it remains slightly below the GDMI and HCCA aids. In 72 
hours, wind shear is forecast to increase and the system will move 
into a slightly drier mid-level air mass. Thus, a weakening trend is 
shown at that time.
